5
A toy car travels on a circular track at a constant speed of 0.50 m s–1. It passes a point on the
track at time t = 0 and takes a time of 40 s to travel once around the track.
The magnitude of the average velocity of the car between t = 0 and t = 20 s is v20.
The magnitude of the average velocity of the car between t = 0 and t = 40 s is v40.
What are v20 and v40?
v20 / m s–1
v40 / m s–1
A
0.32
0
B
0.32
0.32
C
0.50
0
D
0.50
0.50

hints: Notice the times: 40 s is one full lap and 20 s is exactly half a lap, so think about where the car is relative to the start in each case.
Recall average velocity is displacement divided by time, $v_{av} = \Delta x / \Delta t$, while the given $0.50 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ is speed along the curved distance.
First find the track circumference from $0.50 \text{ m s}^{-1} \times 40 \text{ s}$, then use it to get the straight-line displacement for the half-lap at 20 s.
walkthrough: Average velocity magnitude is $\lvert \Delta x \rvert / \Delta t$, where $\Delta x$ is the straight-line displacement from the $t=0$ point, not the distance travelled along the track.
Find the circumference $C$ from constant speed: $C = v \times T = 0.50 \text{ m s}^{-1} \times 40 \text{ s} = 20 \text{ m}$.
Between $t=0$ and $t=20$ s is half a period, so the car is on the opposite side of the circle. Displacement equals the diameter $d = C/\pi = 20/\pi \text{ m} \approx 6.37 \text{ m}$.
Hence $v_{20} = d/20 = (20/\pi)/20 = 1/\pi \text{ m s}^{-1} \approx 0.32 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ with units $\text{m s}^{-1}$.
Between $t=0$ and $t=40$ s is one full lap, so the final position equals the initial position. Displacement is $0$, so $v_{40} = 0/40 = 0$.
The pair $0.32 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $0$ is option A.

A.explanation: Average velocity uses displacement. Half lap gives $v_{20} \approx 0.32 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and full lap gives zero displacement so $v_{40}=0$.

B.explanation: The $0.32 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ value is correct for 20 s, but after 40 s the car is back at the start so displacement and average velocity are zero.

C.explanation: 0.50 is the constant speed, not the magnitude of average velocity over half a circle where displacement is the diameter, shorter than the arc length.

D.explanation: Both values confuse speed with velocity. Average velocity needs straight-line displacement, which is less than distance for 20 s and zero for 40 s.
